proposals: CBDT should publish yearly statistics of capital-gains tax on listed equity and equity funds, split into short- and long-term gains and by taxpayers’ income band, so the argument that the 2024 rate changes land hardest on small, patient savers can be tested against data.

SEBI should repeat and publish every year its study of individual traders’ profits and losses in equity derivatives, before and after delta-based position limits, so the balance between protecting small traders and shutting them out is judged on measured outcomes.

NSE and BSE should publish monthly the share of trades and turnover in eligible stocks settled on the optional T+0 cycle against T+1, so uptake of same-day settlement across the top 500 stocks is known before it is scaled further.

SEBI should publish each year the number of registered investment advisers and research analysts, with new registrations, surrenders and cancellations, so whether the base of registered advisers is shrinking or recovering can be tracked alongside enforcement against unregistered finfluencers.
